Great coverage of this case. 
As an avid true crime enthusiast, it is funny to me that so many of the channels I watch are now covering the Desi story. 
I am Australian, and have lived in Victoria for over 30 years. 
This guy was nobody. He may have been known to police and locals inside his small town but his infamy never stretched beyond that until this case. In reality, the majority of Victoria, of Australia, had never of Desi Freeman before in their lives. Now he will go down in history as one of Australia's most famous criminals. So insane. 
I remember while he was on the run, there were so many conspiracy theories going around the general public, beliefs that the police actually had Desi in their custody the whole time and they were either holding him against his will and torturing him, or they had already killed him not long after he had shot their co-workers.
(A crazy conspiracist, nutjob suddenly guns down some cops in a country that is not used to gun violence, he is then loose in the wild, and suddenly the whole country tunes into the paranoia and start spreading their own conspiracy theories 😂) 
The media coverage was so wide-spread and so in your face, day after day after day, that you couldn't escape the talk about Desi Freeman. Even during social gatherings his name would come up and people would start a game of "What Would You Do If:" and then ask something like "...if you ran into Desi Freeman and he asked you for help?" Some people answered jokingly or sarcastically, offering some exaggerated story about themselves suddenly being closet super hero's or maybe a secret hit man, (just to give a couple of ideas about the sarcastic humour so many of us Aussies seem to use in abundance 😂)
Some would answer seriously, often stating that if it came down to it, they probably would help, mostly due to their fear of saying no to a crazy person that has already killed people!
Some were surprised to hear a lot of people go on to say that they would NOT inform police or attempt to obtain any reward money - their logic being a sound "who in the hell would want to mess with someone crazy enough to shoot and kill cops?!" 
And honestly, who can argue with that?

Regardless of everything though, it's safe to say that we are all genuinely glad to have put all that madness to an end.

And, just quietly, for those of you wondering, yes, the majority of us are 100% convinced that the cops never intended to wear their body cams for Desi's capture. 
Every aussie knows you don't kill bikies and you don't kill cops, both organisations take it highly personally and treat their own as immediate family. Knowing that Desi had already killed 2 of their own, there was no way in hell they were ever going to catch him without killing him.
